questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to increase the distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass if you can. Speeding up will not help. The other driver may just tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: Which color clothing helps you be seen better?
questions.explanation: Wear orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to be seen better on a motorcycle. Wear bright colors anytime you ride, day or night.

questions.question: Gloves can:

options.text: Make it harder to control the motorcycle and should be avoided.
Give you a better grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves help you grip the handlebars better. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, you should:

options.text: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
Ride the same way as when you ride alone.
Make sure footrests are only for you, the rider.
Tell the passenger what to do after you start riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
questions.explanation: Only carry a passenger if your motorcycle is ready for it. Your motorcycle needs a large seat for two people, separate footrests for the passenger, and proper adjustments. You may need to adjust the headlight, tire pressure, and suspension for the extra weight.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to handle differently while riding, you should:

options.text: Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over and check the chain.
Pull over and check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A sudden change in how the motorcycle handles often means a tire has failed. Pull over safely and check your tires if you feel a change in handling.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should wear a jacket:

options.text: No matter what the weather is.
Only for rides longer than half an hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter what the weather is.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you from the sun and dehydration.

questions.question: You should do a full check of your motorcycle:
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent checks than cars. Check your motorcycle completely before every ride.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: Wearing a good-quality helmet greatly reduces head and neck injuries. A helmet is your best protection in an accident.

questions.question: Which type of material offers the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather provides the best protection for motorcycle riders. Always wear clothing that covers your arms and legs completely.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about dangerous road conditions ahead.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane while following a car, what happens?

options.text: You are in the best position to be seen.
The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
The driver will most likely know you are there.
You stop other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
questions.explanation: When riding behind a car, ride in the center of the lane. This way, the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirror much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: When braking, which brakes should you use?

options.text: Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time. The brakes work best when you use them together.

questions.question: What material should riding gloves be made of for the best protection?
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another durable material to protect your hands.

questions.question: What should motorcycle riders wear for clothing?

options.text: Loose clothes that flap in the wind.
Clothes that do not cover your arms or legs completely.
Clothes that can protect you if you crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clothes that can protect you if you crash.
questions.explanation: The right clothing can protect you in a crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely, even on warm days. Your clothes should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind, but not so tight that they limit your movement.

questions.question: Which surface is NOT slippery?

options.text: A strip of oil in the center of a lane.

questions.explanation: Many surfaces have poor grip for tires. These include wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, oil, and metal covers. Dry pavement has much better grip.

questions.question: How should you check your tire pressure?

options.text: Compare the height of your tire to another tire.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check your tire pressure before every ride. A tire that is not full enough may still look fine, so you cannot rely on just looking at it.

questions.question: If a car is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Ride faster to get away from them.
Ride on the shoulder of the road.

questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them get in front of you. If you can do it safely, change lanes and let them pass. Riding faster may make things more dangerous by encouraging them to keep tailgating at the higher speed.

questions.question: What is the single most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened is the single most effective action you can take to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: What should you do about checking your mirrors?

options.text: Check them only on long trips.
Check them regularly as part of your routine.
They are not helpful since you cannot do anything about what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check them regularly as part of your routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your normal routine. Also check them before you change lanes, stop at an intersection, or slow down.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, what should a motorcycle operator be ready for?

options.text: A car suddenly pulling out of a parking space into traffic.
Other drivers seeing you and staying out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car suddenly pulling out of a parking space into traffic.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, be ready for a car to suddenly pull out of a parking space into traffic. It is safer to ride on the left side of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you more space between your motorcycle and any hazards.

questions.question: How can a rider prevent fatigue on long trips?

options.text: Complete the ride with as few stops as possible.
Use caffeine or other artificial stimulants.
Travel as far as possible in one day.

questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from heat, rain, wind, and snow. Ride no more than six hours per day. Stop to rest at least once every two hours. Do not use caffeine or other stimulants, as you may feel very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing helps drivers see you in all conditions. Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight, so wear bright clothing during the day too.

questions.question: What should you do while riding?

options.text: Look ahead and watch for potential dangers.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Do not worry about hazards because there are very few on the road.
Look ahead, but do not look for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and watch for potential dangers.
questions.explanation: Look far ahead while riding to spot possible hazards early. This gives you time to react before you reach them.

questions.question: What should you do with your headlight during the day?

options.text: Turn it on only when it is cloudy.
Use it if you think it helps.

questions.explanation: Always keep your headlight on while riding, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to notice you.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a bridge grating?

options.text: Always ride on the far right side of the lane.
Always ride on the far left side of the lane.
Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may make your motorcycle weave slightly. This is normal and not dangerous. Simply relax and ride at a steady speed. Do not zigzag to fight the weave, as this is unsafe and forces you out of your lane.
